pages.text: $(thing)Sky anomaly pages$() describe impossible things that live in the skybox: auroras, rainbows, shooting stars, comets, rifts, nebulae, glyphs, galaxies, prism rings, lanterns, fracture webs, celestial script, bright or dark skies, and stranger lights besides.

Most of these pages are visual and add no chunk structures. $(thing)Meteor Showers$() and $(thing)Sky Spheres$() are exceptions: they generate physical features. Motes, ash, spores, and void particles are a separate ambient family rendered around travelers.

An authored visual sky anomaly lowers instability by roughly 8 to 12 points, depending on the page. The Age knows what mood its heavens are meant to wear, so it improvises less. A sky anomaly gained through Random receives no authored relief.

Sparse Ages are more likely to grow sky anomalies on their own. Missing terrain, biome, time, weather, sun, moon, and star pages leave silence in the book, and the ink often fills silence with spectacle.
$(item)Lost Pages$() now favor sky anomaly pages more often than before. They are a good way to give an Age identity without asking the server to build another ruin, city, or floating object field.
